how_to_read.similarity: How alike the Earth point and its lunar twin are, 0 to 100, from the mission's variables compared within stated tolerances.
how_to_read.suitability: How well the Earth point meets the mission's own needs as a test site, 0 to 100, from its weighted criteria.
how_to_read.final: The ranking score: half similarity and half suitability (alpha 0.5).
how_to_read.rules: Rover and Solar panels pair on real values within tolerances; Lunar base pairs on thermal position (coldest temperature and daily swing ranked within each world's own population) plus slope and roughness in real values.
how_to_read.levels: MEASURED = from a named measured product; DERIVED = a stated formula on measured values; MODELLED = a model or climatology, not a measurement of the cell (variables.json).
how_to_read.percentile_words: Words such as gentle, smooth, coldest are used only when both sides fall in the same quarter (or tenth) of their own population; the population is named in each trait's basis.

caveats: Each place is a 1-degree cell, about 111 km north-south on Earth (about 30 km on the Moon); values are cell averages.
Earth temperatures and ground sunlight are modelled climatologies (WorldClim, MODIS-based amplitude, modelled irradiance), not site measurements.
Names are the nearest named feature or populated place to the cell centre, not a landing site or the cell's own name.
Lunar base pairs are a likeness of thermal position within each world's population, not of temperature: the real temperatures are about 200 K apart.
Sunlight above the atmosphere is alike for Solar panels pairs, but on Earth a large share is lost in the atmosphere; panels would not charge the same.

variables.label: Daily temperature swing (position)
variables.c_note: a temperature difference: 1 K = 1 degree C, so the swing in degrees C equals the value in K

pairs.pair_sentence_from_bundle: This pair matches by relative thermal position, not by equal temperatures: this site's coldest temperature and daily swing rank among Earth's lunar-base candidates where its twin's rank among the cells of NASA's nine candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole. In real values the twin is 195 K colder on average (minimum -232 °C at the surface against -24.5 °C air temperature here) and its day-night swing is 138 K larger; slope differs by 0.5° and roughness by 0.3 m.

common_traits.text: Both rank in the coldest tenth of their own population by coldest temperature (8th percentile on Earth, 8th on the Moon, 0.3 points apart), although the temperatures themselves are far apart: about -25 degrees C air on Earth against -232 degrees C surface on the Moon, 207 K.

populations.EARTH: 2,419 Earth points passing the Lunar base funnel
populations.MOON: 280 lunar cells of NASA's nine candidate regions
